name: Fletcherizing

card.summary: Chewing each mouthful until it is liquid before swallowing, a century-old diet habit that some looksmaxxers link to jaw muscle use and leanness.
card.note: Jaw fatigue and pain can follow prolonged chewing.

quick.overview:
Fletcherizing, also called Fletcherism, is the practice of chewing food until it is thoroughly liquefied before swallowing. It was promoted from the 1890s by American Horace Fletcher, who claimed it improved health and let people eat less.

In appearance terms, its followers have linked it to eating less, which may support leanness, and chewing is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to use the jaw muscles. Medical commentators of Fletcher's time and later have been critical of his broader health claims.
quick.how: Practitioners slow down their eating and chew each bite many more times than usual, sometimes aiming for a set number of chews, until the food is a pulp. Fletcher also advised sipping liquids rather than gulping and eating only when hungry.
quick.risks: Prolonged chewing can produce jaw muscle fatigue and pain. Experts have also criticised the movement's strong health claims.

lead: Fletcherizing, or Fletcherism, is a chewing-based eating system named for Horace Fletcher (1849-1919), an American food writer who taught that food should be chewed until liquefied before swallowing [1].

Fletcher said the method would let people gain strength while eating less, and he promoted it as a route to better digestion and health [1]. Because it slows eating and reduces intake, followers have connected it to leanness, and in modern looksmaxxing talk extended chewing is also associated with working the jaw muscles.

The movement attracted notable followers, including Upton Sinclair, Henry James and John D. Rockefeller, and was studied at Yale by Russell Chittenden [1]. Medical experts of the time described it as faddism, and the article-level record notes that its extreme claims lack scientific support [1].

chain: Meals slow down and intake may fall
Leaner physique; more jaw muscle activity
angle.text: Fletcher's followers used slow chewing to eat less while feeling satisfied, which can support a leaner look. Some looksmaxxers also associate extended chewing with working the jaw muscles.

paras: Horace Fletcher, born in Lawrence, Massachusetts in 1849, developed his method to address his own dyspepsia and weight and became wealthy lecturing on it. His books included Menticulture (1896) and Fletcherism, What It Is (1913) [1].
He died of bronchitis in Copenhagen in 1919 [1].

Fletcher summarised the approach as eating only with a good appetite, chewing food to a pulp and sipping liquids [1]. He claimed it would increase strength on less food and aid conditions ranging from colitis to alcoholism [1]. Some accounts describe chewing a mouthful up to a hundred times [1].

Contemporary medical figures called Fletcher a food faddist, and critics nicknamed the movement the "chew-chew cult". Carl Malmberg warned that a near-liquid diet lacked bulk and might cause constipation [1].
A randomised study found that 40 or 60 minutes of continuous gum chewing induced marked subjective jaw-muscle fatigue lasting up to 20 minutes afterwards in healthy volunteers [2].

No studies found on Fletcherizing itself. A randomised trial of 31 healthy adults used prolonged gum chewing as a model for jaw muscle pain and fatigue, showing that extended chewing can tire the jaw muscles [2].
